key_insight: ESPINN can infer both the bulk chemical potential and gradient coefficients of phase-field models from sparse transient snapshots, including very limited data.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-efficient, physically consistent way to identify constitutive laws for phase separation and microstructure evolution when parameters are unknown.
method: Uses an extended pseudo-spectral physics-informed neural network to solve the inverse problem.
Learns both free-energy structure and interfacial gradient terms from snapshot pairs.
Tests recovery on the 1D Cahn-Hilliard equation under noiseless and noisy conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate and statistically stable reconstruction in the noiseless case, with improved robustness as more snapshots are used under noise.
watch_item: Reconstruction accuracy degrades with noise, so practical use may require multiple snapshots and careful noise handling.
paper_title: Extended pseudo-spectral physics-informed neural networks for phase-field models
